records.headline: Operators optimize for CTR and FTDs.
records.post_text:
Operators optimize for CTR and FTDs.
But performance starts earlier: with audience intent.

That's where FSM is shifting.

We're looking less at "sports audience" as one big group and more at actual behavior:

who checks odds before a match,
who follows live updates,
who comes back to the same league or team,
who spends time on stats pages.

Those groups behave differently. So they should be bought differently.

Direct deals still give you access to the publisher network. 
Programmatic helps scale the segments that show intent. 
Our DMP is where that audience behavior gets organized before you scale.

This means the learner buys with less budget drained.

#FSM #CTR #sportsaudience #sportstraffic #WorldCup2026

more_relevant_posts.post_text: Major sporting events don’t just attract fans. They reshape audiences in real time. Yet most sports marketing strategies are still built on static segments and outdated assumptions. In this byline for Association of National Advertisers , Mateusz Jędrocha , CPO at Adlook, explores why marketers keep missing the biggest audience shifts during moments like the Super Bowl or World Cup - and what needs to change. If audiences are dynamic, your strategy should be too. Read more: https://lnkd.in/dJDVTxYJ #Adlook #AdTech #SportsMarketing #Programmatic #CTV
to my sports leads, this really explains how a quality DSP strategy is a force multiplier with major event campaigns

Millions of views look great on a quarterly report, but do they translate into Steam wishlists? In the Latin American gaming market, many global campaigns fall into the trap of vanity metrics. Hiring mega-influencers might give your game temporary visibility, but without niche alignment and data-driven attribution, you are likely overpaying on your User Acquisition Cost (CAC). At Keyframe, we bypass the noise. We analyze audience sentiment, tracking retention and direct community conversions rather than just surface-level clicks. True media performance isn't about spending more; it's about making every single dollar count where the local audience actually converts. #DataDrivenPR #UserAcquisition #GamingIndustry #LatAmMarket #ROI

World Cup viewing habits are evolving in real time. From free streaming matches to highlight reels and rising out-of-home viewership, Nexxen's latest research report uncovers how economic pressures are reshaping audience behavior. And for advertisers, understanding these shifts is key to building smarter media plans and driving incremental reach, no matter where fans tune in. Read more and download the full report before the World Cup kicks off (pun intended!) later this month. https://lnkd.in/eAzGtBGF

⚽ With the World cup only a few days away, economic pressure isn’t reducing World Cup interest, but it is changing how people plan to watch. Nexxen ’s latest FIFA World Cup 2026 Predictions and Insights Report highlights a more fragmented, flexible viewing landscape, with audiences moving across free streaming, vMVPDs, out-of-home environments and highlights-led content. A few standout findings: ⚽ 14 million Americans who previously did not plan to watch now say they will tune in after learning Tubi will stream select marquee matches for free 📺 40% of consumers plan to add a subscription service to watch the tournament 🍻 9 million more fans now expect to watch in free out-of-home environments such as bars and restaurants 📱 19 million won’t watch matches live, but will still engage through highlights, recaps, creator content and wider tournament coverage For advertisers, the message is clear: major sports moments are no longer just about live reach. They are about understanding where, when and how audiences engage across an increasingly fragmented viewing journey. That makes data, identity resolution and cross-channel measurement more important than ever. Read the report here: https://lnkd.in/e4QXXfj2 #WorldCup2026 #CTV #SportsMarketing #AdTech #Programmatic #Nexxen

CTV campaigns with tight geo, audience, and programming requirements often run into the same challenge: rising costs and limited scale. That was the case for stackrabbit and John Moore Services as they looked to drive awareness and site visits across premium CTV environments. Peer39 categories across Premium Services, Home & Garden, Live Sports, and Local News inventory improved efficiency while maintaining quality and control over where ads appeared. The results: ⬆️ 22% improvement in media efficiency 🏠 Lower cost-per-site-visit 🔍 Greater transparency and control over where ads ran A strong example of how better signals and smarter targeting can improve CTV performance. 🌟 See how the strategy came together: https://lnkd.in/g_pBJyZT

Download our latest benchmarking report! Two key takeaways: 1. Audience continues to decline for many publishers 📉 However, top-performers are seeing growth despite broad shifts in consumer behavior and reduced referrals from platforms Certainly Google Zero and AI are part of the story but the trend started years ago. Is it also a content, engagement/relevance, technology, and product problem? 2. Revenue growth is being driven mostly by rising ARPU for print and digital subscriptions 📈 Most publishers are reaching a subscription plateau with minimal volume growth Finding new revenue streams (such as monetizing agents) and continuing to raise ARPU (while adding value to consumers and introducing new product tiers) will be common themes in 2026. #agenticweb

One of the more interesting dynamics in North American news media right now: Audience pressure continues, but revenue performance remains relatively resilient. Mather’s latest benchmarking report shows: 📉 Traffic: -12% 📈 Conversion efficiency: +33% 📈 ARPU: +7.1% The industry is increasingly being forced to do more with a smaller audience. Which raises an important question for Europe as well: If audience growth continues to slow, will long-term sustainability increasingly depend on retention, pricing and ARPU growth instead?
